newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged but firm tone.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged but firm tone.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were mostly unchanged in quiet trading Monday, but traders said they saw signs of a slightly better tone.

"There was a minor upward bias," one muni trader said near the close. He attributed the better tone to the extremely thin supply levels of recent weeks, and said this week's $3 billion of deals would not be enough to hurt the technical picture.
A market analyst said he thought some prices might have edged up about 1/8 point on the day, but most issues were essentially unchanged.

In Monday's new issue pricings, Goldman Sachs & Co said it repriced Tacoma, Wash.'s $101.5 million electric system revenue refunding bonds, changing coupons in several maturities. The top yield was 5.55 percent in 2015.
Tuesday's deals total $1.2 billion in 37 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $413 million in 24 sales. The largest is a $143 million Industry Urban Development, Calif., deal at 1400 EST.
Negotiated sales total $770 million in 13 offerings. The largest is a $260 million Jefferson County, Ala., issue through Raymond James & Associates Inc.

Tuesday also features the start of the Treasury's quarterly refunding, with the the sale of $17.75 billion of three-year notes. On Wednesday comes a $12 billion 10-year sale, and a $10 billion 30-year sale on Thursday.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 3/32 to 116-1/32 while March T-bonds were unchanged at 112-15/32. The MOB spread was 114 ticks widening from 111 at the close on Friday.
In the secondary market, bids on Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were up two basis points to 5.64 percent net.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 lost one basis point, moving to 5.74 percent net after being quoted earlier Monday at a 5.77 percent.
